notes:
Two bullets and two sub-bullets, and the sub-bullets are the whole shape of the quest: this is a two-step errand for a veteran and a five-step one for a first-timer, and nothing in a packet says which you are. Steps 3 to 5 are therefore marked optional -- they are conditional on this being your first Trust quest, not a ladder position everyone climbs.

Steps 3 and 4 are ALTERNATIVES, not a set: the page says the Trust spell may be cast in EITHER South or North Gustaberg. They are given a shared group so both are drawn at once, which is the right guidance for an OR even though 'group' nominally means an unordered AND. Neither is a talk or a trade, so both are kind 'other' targeting the zone itself -- what the player has to do is be standing in Gustaberg.

The Blue institute card is in the header's Reward list, which normally disqualifies it as evidence, but bullet 1 says outright that Clarion Star hands it over at the start. The reward table here is really 'everything this quest yields', and the walkthrough is the more specific statement, so the card is used as step 1's evidence. The Bastok Trust permit is genuinely a completion reward -- it is what you get at the END of either branch -- so it is not evidence anywhere. Blue and Green institute cards are distinct key items, so there is no cross-talk with Trust: Windurst.

'Level 5+ on any Job' is the level gate restated for any job, so jobs stays empty. The header gives no grid for Clarion Star; bullet 1 does, so (K-7) is recovered from the walkthrough and start.raw is kept verbatim.

notes:
Three bullets, and the middle two are one act: find the Warhorse Hoofprint and click it. What makes this worth splitting is the sub-bullet -- there is ONE hoofprint and it can be in any of four zones, and since the December 2015 update it shows on widescan. Four group members, one per zone, all drawn at once, is the only honest way to say 'it is in exactly one of these and we cannot tell you which'. It is an OR rather than the AND a group usually means, which is flagged.

The Dark Rider hoofprint key item goes on the LAST group member, not on all four: duplicate evidence across steps is a hard gate, and putting it last means satisfying it lands the mark on Naja rather than back inside the group. That follows An Explorer's Footsteps.

The header writes the giver's grid as '(1-10)' -- a digit one where the letter I belongs. Every other page in the corpus puts Naja Salaheem at Aht Urhgan Whitegate (I-10), so that is what is recorded; start.raw keeps the typo verbatim.

'Complete 25 points worth of Assaults as Private First Class' has no slot in the schema and no observable predicate, so it gates nothing and is flagged.

notes:
Six bullets, five steps: bullet 4 is a count and a hint ('seven total crates, only three give an item, one hides behind the Maw exit') attached to bullet 3's search, not an action of its own.

The three key items are the cleanest evidence in this batch -- all three are granted at the trunks and nowhere else, the header's Reward is 'None' so there is no reward collision, and they are gone by the time Raibaht is done with you. They therefore sit as a single AND-list on step 3 and reappear as step 4's items, which is what you must be holding to hand them over.

The page writes the object plural, 'Repair Trunks', because there are seven of them; the entity name is recorded singular. That is a reading, not a verification -- there is no entity table to check it against, hence the flag.

Everything happens around (I-13) in one zone, so this is a very short walk despite being five rungs. Fame code 'akon' is an Abyssea zone code, not one of the nine regions, so it gates nothing; the raw string is kept.

The four Signboards are explicitly 'go around to' them, with four grid refs and no order, so they share a group and all four draw at once. Each needs the poster key item in hand, which is why it is listed as items on all four rather than as evidence on any of them.

The page writes the key item plural, 'Hastily scrawled posters'. The game's name is singular, 'Hastily scrawled poster' (key item 1596); the plural does not resolve at all, so the singular is what is recorded. It is granted when Bopa Greso hands out the job, so it is step 1's evidence.

The trailing 'Zoning is required to repeat this quest' is a repeat condition, not a step -- and nothing in a packet reports a zone change against a quest, so it is only a note.

notes:
Three bullets, three steps, and the interesting decision is what NOT to use as evidence. Regine hands you three Hatchets, which looks like a clean step 1 latch until the sub-bullet says 'You can bring your own Hatchets obtained by other means' -- a Hatchet is a common woodworking tool and holding one proves nothing about this quest. Step 1 therefore has no evidence.

The Plateau Chestnuts do work: three of them, obtained only by logging, and they are handed straight to Rugiette. They are step 2's evidence and step 3's items, which is the Operation Teatime shape. The header writes 'Plat. Chestnut Plateau Chestnut x3' -- the wiki's icon name followed by the long name; both resolve to item 2608 and the long form is used.

The logging points are given as regions of the map rather than grid refs ('between Conflux #01 and #02, around Puks, West/South of Conflux #07 and in the Opo-opo'), so step 2 gets a zone and no grid. 'Logging Point' is the object name and is a reading of the sub-bullet's plural, not something verifiable here.

Fame code 'alth' is an Abyssea zone code and gates nothing. The trailing 'Zoning is not required to repeat this quest' is a repeat condition, not a step.

The nine waypoints are a set with no order, so they share a group and all nine draw at once. The parenthetical names the page gives them ('Peacekeepers' Coalition', 'The auction house', 'Castle Adoulin gates') are place descriptions, not entity names, so each is a Waypoint at its grid ref with the description in the note.

notes:
Ten bullets and five steps. Bullets 3, 4, 5, 6 and 8 are turn-by-turn directions through Sea Serpent Grotto -- 'head South until the fork at (H-6), head East', 'turn South at (J-5)' -- and none of them is a thing you do to an entity. They fold into the travel step and the examine step as notes; a verb scan would have produced five bogus rungs out of them.

Bullet 7 is the one that looks like routing and is not: the Silver Door at (N-14) is a real targetable object, and getting through it means examining it three times and then trading a Silver Beastcoin. The page is explicit that you KEEP the coin, so it is items on the step and never evidence -- holding a Silver Beastcoin says nothing about how far along you are, and the coin is also listed under Item Reqs for that reason.

The Sea serpent statue at the ??? at (H-3) is the only observable thing in the quest and is the natural anchor: hold it and the mark belongs back on Laisrean. The ??? itself keeps its rung even though it can never carry a marker.

'Anything will do' in the description is flavour -- the walkthrough names exactly one thing to fetch.

notes:
Four numbered bullets and only two of them are the quest. Bullets 3 and 4 sit under a 'Note:' heading and are about what the Mistmelt REWARD does afterwards -- forcing Ouryu out of the sky, and having no effect in The Savage II. They are consequences of finishing, not steps, and a keyword pass would have made a step out of 'force Ouryu out of the sky'.

What is left is talk, then trade, both on Ferchinne in one spot -- the same shape as A Feather in One's Cap. No separate gathering step is recorded for the tailfeathers: the page offers two Riverne zones OR the auction house, so there is no single place to point at, and wedging an unmarkable rung between two steps on the same NPC would break the marker run for nothing. Holding two feathers already reads as ready-to-hand-in through step 2's items.

'Quest Reqs: Promathia Mission 4-2' has no slot in the schema and no observable predicate, so it gates nothing and is flagged. Fame 'Other' is not one of the nine regions and gates nothing either. The page is tagged Category:Disambiguation but carries only the Tavnazian Safehold quest, so identity is untouched.
